edges.description: ADE-driven immune activation and cytokine dysregulation contribute to the vascular permeability underlying severe-dengue plasma leakage.
edges.source: Antibody-Dependent Enhancement in Secondary Heterotypic Infection

edges.description: Stripping the endothelial glycocalyx removes a principal regulator of endothelial barrier function, and the resulting hyperpermeability is the cell-intrinsic mechanism of plasma leakage.

When leakage is severe enough, the loss of circulating volume produces hypovolemic shock. Splitting this from the leakage node matters therapeutically: fluid resuscitation acts on the volume loss, not on the permeability that caused it.
Hypovolemic shock arising from dengue plasma leakage is the clinical presentation named dengue shock syndrome.
Activated platelets are cleared faster than they are replaced, which is what the falling platelet count measures.
edges.source: Platelet Activation and Accelerated Platelet Clearance

edges.description: Platelet depletion contributes to the bleeding tendency, alongside the disordered hemostasis reported in severe dengue. The intermediates are not resolved here, so the link is not typed as direct.
edges.source: Platelet Activation and Accelerated Platelet Clearance

edges.description: Excessive or unbalanced complement activation is proposed to increase vascular permeability and drive the plasma leakage that defines severe dengue. The intermediates linking complement activation products to endothelial barrier failure are not established in this cohort.

nodes.description: Transcriptional signature of complement dysregulation in pediatric dengue: classical and lectin pathway components are upregulated during primary infection with concurrent downregulation of several complement regulators (FDR-significant). The primary-versus-secondary comparison shows a nominal trend toward the reciprocal pattern (C1QA/C1QC/C2/C4b down, CFI/C4BP/MBL2/CFP up), which the authors interpret as a transition from activation to regulation in secondary infection, though this comparison did not reach FDR significance.

evidence.reference_title: Bulk transcriptomics of peripheral blood mononuclear cells delineates systems-level immune dysregulation in pediatric dengue infection.
evidence.snippet: Multiple classical and lectin pathway genes were upregulated in the primary dengue cohort, including MBL2, C1QA, C1QB, C1QC, C2, and C9 (Fig. 3). In contrast, several complement regulatory factors were downregulated in the primary dengue cohort, including CD93, properdin (CFP), CR1, SERPING, C4BPA, C4BPB, and CFD

evidence.reference_title: Bulk transcriptomics of peripheral blood mononuclear cells delineates systems-level immune dysregulation in pediatric dengue infection.
evidence.snippet: Further analysis of the primary vs secondary dengue cohort data revealed a widespread downregulation of C1QA, C1QC, C2, and C4b accompanied by upregulation of CFI, C4BP, MBL2, and CFP, which suggests a transition from activation to regulation

nodes.description: Dengue-specific IgA antibodies provide protection through direct neutralization and blockade of IgG-mediated antibody-dependent enhancement. The absence of enhanced inflammation is reported for human macrophage cultures exposed to IgA-DENV complexes, and does not extend to IgA responses generally: anti-NS1 IgA raised by prior Zika infection is associated with increased risk of severe DENV-2 disease through neutrophil Fc-alpha receptor engagement.

nodes.description: Secreted dengue NS1 acts directly on vascular endothelium: it induces sialidase and heparanase expression and activates cathepsin L, which together strip sialic acid and shed heparan sulfate proteoglycans from the endothelial glycocalyx layer. Loss of that layer is an endothelial cell-intrinsic route to hyperpermeability, separate from the antibody- and cytokine-mediated arm above.

evidence.reference_title: Dengue Virus NS1 Disrupts the Endothelial Glycocalyx, Leading to Hyperpermeability.
evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that DENV NS1 disrupts the EGL on human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells, inducing degradation of sialic acid and shedding of heparan sulfate proteoglycans.

evidence.reference_title: Dengue Virus NS1 Disrupts the Endothelial Glycocalyx, Leading to Hyperpermeability.
evidence.snippet: This effect is mediated by NS1-induced expression of sialidases and heparanase, respectively.

nodes.description: Increased vascular permeability allows plasma to escape the intravascular compartment into the pleural and peritoneal spaces, with hemoconcentration. This is the pathophysiological hallmark that separates dengue hemorrhagic fever from uncomplicated dengue fever.

evidence.snippet: Plasma leakages is the main pathophysiological hallmark that distinguishes DHF from DF.

nodes.description: Circulating platelets carry DENV genome and become activated, acquiring surface complement C3 and IgG and being phagocytosed by monocytes. Platelet counts fall around day 4 of fever and recover from day 6 to day 10, tracking the activation markers.

nodes.description: Active immunization with tetravalent live-attenuated dengue vaccines — the DENV-2-backboned TAK-003 (Qdenga) or the yellow fever 17D-backboned chimeric CYD-TDV (Dengvaxia) — elicits neutralizing antibodies against all four DENV serotypes and, for TAK-003, non-structural protein (NS1) humoral and cellular immunity that limits viremia and prevents severe endothelial glycocalyx disruption. Clinical deployment is critically modified by baseline dengue serostatus: CYD-TDV lacks DENV NS1 antigens and sensitized baseline-seronegative vaccinees to antibody-dependent enhancement and increased hospitalization risk upon primary wild-type infection, restricting its indication to laboratory-confirmed seropositive individuals, whereas TAK-003 demonstrated 4.5-year efficacy and safety against all four serotypes in baseline-seropositive individuals and against DENV-1 and DENV-2 in baseline-seronegative individuals.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term efficacy and safety of a tetravalent dengue vaccine (TAK-003): 4·5-year results from a phase 3, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
evidence.snippet: TAK-003 demonstrated long-term efficacy and safety against all four DENV serotypes in previously exposed individuals and against DENV-1 and DENV-2 in dengue-naive individuals.

evidence.reference_title: Safety issues from a Phase 3 clinical trial of a live-attenuated chimeric yellow fever tetravalent dengue vaccine.
evidence.snippet: In response to the recognized vulnerability of seronegatives, on 29 November 2017, Sanofi issued a press release stating that “For individuals who have not been previously infected by dengue virus, vaccination should not be recommended.”

evidence.reference_title: Dengue virus: epidemiology, biology, and disease aetiology.
evidence.snippet: Clinical symptoms of dengue range from mild fever to severe dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) or dengue shock syndrome (DSS), with thrombocytopenia, leucopenia, and increased vascular permeability.
